title: Ivo and the Signal
premise: Jonah Blackwood, a navigator who fled a corporate massacre ten years ago, is hauling contraband medical supplies when the Meridian returns from deep space with its crew aged backward and no memory of the atrocity that launched them. Aboard is Sefa, the ship's AI fragment carrying encrypted proof of the massacre — proof that implicates Jonah's own former captain, now a fleet admiral rewriting history in real time. As the reactor aboard the derelict Meridian counts toward detonation and bounty hunters close in, Jonah's ragtag crew must choose between selling the evidence for their own survival or broadcasting it and becoming fugitives. In the end they broadcast it, losing their ship and nearly each other, but gaining something rarer: a family bound by truth instead of debt.
about_author: Wren Vasquez is a former radio telescope technician who writes science fiction about people who fix things that were built to be disposable. They live in a converted lighthouse with two cats and an unreasonable number of circuit boards.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Hauling cargo through contested orbits, Jonah avoids the hold where his employer stores cryo-backups of 'terminated' crew — including, he suspects, copies of himself. When a distress ping drags him off-course, he resents the interruption. Emotional beat: numbness cracking into unease as we learn what he's been running from.

chapters.title: The Meridian
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa, Jonah's engineer and de facto conscience. They dock with the derelict Meridian and find its crew alive but decades younger, memories intact up to launch day and blank after. The reactor is counting down on a timer nobody set. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Backups Sleeping
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Among the rejuvenated crew is Tam Okafor, Jonah's old shipmate who died in the Callisto Yard massacre — except Tam doesn't remember dying, or Jonah betraying the escape plan. Emotional beat: guilt made flesh; Jonah can't decide whether to confess or flee again.

chapters.title: Every Record Says Otherwise
chapters.summary: POV Sefa (the AI fragment). Hidden in the Meridian's systems, Sefa reveals corrupted logs: official records show the massacre never happened, only a 'routine decommission.' Someone is editing history from the inside. Emotional beat: cold clarity — the horror isn't the crime, it's its erasure.

chapters.title: The Admiral's Grace
chapters.summary: POV Tam. Fleet Admiral Corvane broadcasts a rescue offer: surrender the Meridian and receive amnesty. Tam, trusting and young-faced, wants to believe. Jonah recognizes Corvane's voice as the captain who ordered the deaths. Emotional beat: hope weaponized; the crew splits over whether to answer.

chapters.title: Countdown Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Working out the reactor timer, Ilsa realizes it's synchronized to Corvane's flagship arrival — the Meridian was meant to be destroyed with all witnesses. Bounty hunters board during the calculation. Emotional beat: desperate competence; found family functioning under fire for the first time.

chapters.title: What We Sold to Survive
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Cornered, Jonah confesses everything: he took payment to open the yard doors, believing the backups would preserve everyone anyway. Tam's forgiveness is worse than anger. Emotional beat: the price of survival named aloud — and refused as an excuse any longer.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The crew commits: transmit the uncorrupted logs fleet-wide before Corvane arrives. Sefa must burn her own core as the antenna amplifier. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely, contrasting every coerced sacrifice in the backstory.

chapters.title: The Reactor Finishes Its Countdown
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Corvane's fleet arrives mid-broadcast; the truth goes out as the Meridian detonates. The crew escapes in a gutted shuttle while Corvane's own officers, hearing the logs, refuse his order to fire. Emotional beat: catharsis through chaos — survival redefined as witness, not escape.

chapters.title: Signal, Received
chapters.summary: POV Tam, months later. The crew drifts between stations, broke and famous, rebuilding a small ship they name Meridian. Tam chooses to stay young-faced among people who know his whole story. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — power corrupts, but truth, once loose, cannot be backed up and deleted.
